skr03.about: SKR03 (Standardkontenrahmen 03) is the DATEV chart of accounts, the most widely used by German small businesses and their tax advisers (Steuerberater). Accounts have 4 digits and follow the business process. VAT has one account per rate: output VAT (Umsatzsteuer) 1776 (19%) and 1771 (7%), input VAT (Vorsteuer) 1576 (19%) and 1571 (7%). Amounts in euros (€).

terms.debit: Debit: value coming into an account. For an asset account (bank, inventory), debiting = increasing. For a liability account, debiting = decreasing.
terms.credit: Credit: value leaving an account. For an asset account, crediting = decreasing. For a liability or equity account, crediting = increasing.
terms.journal: Journal: chronological record of all accounting transactions. Every entry must be balanced (Total debit = Total credit).
terms.compte: Account: a numbered bucket that tracks the movements of one item (bank, VAT, customer, supplier…). Your business uses {{plan}}.
terms.plan_comptable: Chart of accounts: the standardized list of accounts. Your business uses {{plan}}. {{classes}}
terms.tva: VAT: tax collected on behalf of the government ({{vat}}% for you). VAT collected (account {{account}}): what you owe the government.
terms.tvaDeductible: Recoverable VAT (account {{account}}): what you can deduct.
terms.salesTax: Sales tax: collected on behalf of the tax authority (account {{account}}).
terms.balance: Trial balance: a table summarizing every account with its debit or credit balance. Used to check that the books are balanced.
terms.bilan: Balance sheet: a snapshot of the business's financial position on a given date. Assets = what the business owns. Liabilities and equity = how it is financed (debts + equity).
terms.compte_de_resultat: Income statement: the story of the business's activity over a period. Revenue (income) - Expenses (costs) = Net income (profit or loss).
terms.charges: Expenses: the business's costs. Purchases of goods ({{achats}}), Salaries ({{salaires}}), Rent ({{loyer}}), Telephone ({{telecom}})…
terms.produits: Revenue: the business's income. Sales of goods ({{ventes}}), Services sold ({{services}})…
terms.immobilisation: Fixed asset: a durable asset used for more than one year (computer, vehicle, premises). Depreciated gradually over its useful life.
terms.amortissement: Depreciation: recording the loss in value of a fixed asset. Example: a computer costing {{amount}} over 3 years = {{perYear}} of expense per year.
terms.grand_livre: General ledger: the detail of all transactions, grouped by account. Lets you trace the complete history of an account.
terms.lettrage: Matching: linking the entries of a customer or supplier account with the corresponding payments.
terms.rapprochement: Bank reconciliation: comparing the bank (or Mobile Money) statement with the books to identify differences.
terms.capitaux_propres: Equity: funding provided by the owners + accumulated earnings. Share capital + Reserves + Net income for the year.
terms.tresorerie: Cash: all available liquid funds (bank + cash on hand + Mobile Money). A healthy balance sheet = positive cash.
terms.resultat: Net income = Total revenue - Total expenses. Positive = profit. Negative = loss. It flows into equity on the balance sheet.

journal_entry.title: Recording a journal entry
journal_entry.intro: A journal entry records a business event. The golden rule: Total debit = Total credit.
journal_entry.doubleEntryText: Every transaction affects at least two accounts in opposite directions. If you buy a computer for {{amount}} paid by bank transfer: you debit the Equipment account ({{materiel}}) and credit the Bank account ({{banque}}).
journal_entry.whenTitle: When to debit, when to credit?
journal_entry.whenText: Asset accounts (bank, cash on hand, Mobile Money, inventory, customers): Debit = increase, Credit = decrease. Liability and Revenue accounts: Debit = decrease, Credit = increase.
journal_entry.exampleSale: Sale of goods {{ht}} excl. tax + VAT {{vat}} to customer Dupont
journal_entry.exampleSaleNoVat: Sale of goods {{ht}} excl. tax to customer Dupont
journal_entry.examplePurchase: Purchase of office supplies {{amount}} paid by Mobile Money
journal_entry.examplePayment: Payment from customer Dupont received in the bank
journal_entry.tip1: If the entry is not balanced, the system flags it in red.
journal_entry.tip2: Invoices, payments and goods receipts created in Procura post their journal entries automatically.
journal_entry.tip3: Choose the right journal: Purchases (ACH), Sales (VTE), Bank (BNQ), Cash and Mobile Money (CAI), Miscellaneous (OD).
journal_entry.exampleSaleReduced: Sale at the reduced {{rate}}% rate (books, food…): {{ht}} net + VAT {{vat}}
journal_entry.examplePurchaseBank: Purchase of office supplies {{amount}} paid by bank transfer

chart_of_accounts.title: Chart of accounts — quick guide
chart_of_accounts.tip1: Create sub-accounts (e.g. {{account}}) to track each customer individually.
chart_of_accounts.tip2: Expense and revenue accounts are reset to zero at year-end (net income).
chart_of_accounts.tip3: An account is "settled" when its total debit = total credit.

balance_sheet.title: Understanding the balance sheet
balance_sheet.intro: The balance sheet is a snapshot of the business's financial position on a specific date: assets on one side, liabilities and equity on the other.
balance_sheet.assetsText: Non-current assets: durable goods (machinery, vehicles). Current assets: inventory, accounts receivable (money owed to you), cash (bank, cash on hand, Mobile Money).
balance_sheet.liabilitiesTitle: Liabilities and equity: how it is financed
balance_sheet.liabilitiesText: Equity: owners' contributions + accumulated profits. Financial debt: bank loans. Operating liabilities: suppliers to pay, VAT and social contributions to remit.
balance_sheet.tip1: A balance sheet always balances: Total assets = Total liabilities and equity. If not, there is an error.
balance_sheet.tip2: A current assets / short-term liabilities ratio > 1 means you can pay your immediate debts.
balance_sheet.tip3: Net income from the income statement shows up in equity on the balance sheet.

general_ledger.title: General ledger — what is it for?
general_ledger.intro: The general ledger groups all journal entries by account. It is the reference tool for finding a specific transaction.
general_ledger.readTitle: How to read a general ledger line
general_ledger.readText: Each line = one entry in a journal. You see the date, the description, the debit or credit amount, and the running balance of the account.
general_ledger.balanceText: Debit balance: normal for Bank, Cash on hand, Customers, Inventory. Credit balance: normal for Suppliers, VAT collected, Capital.
general_ledger.tip1: Filter by account to see the full history of a customer or supplier.
general_ledger.tip2: A settled customer account = all invoices have been paid.

howTo.title: What to do with these numbers
howTo.de: Log in to ELSTER (Mein ELSTER), open the Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung for the period and copy boxes Kz 81, 86 and 66; ELSTER works out box 83. Submit before the deadline and pay the amount to the Finanzamt (or wait for the refund).
howTo.fr: Enter these amounts in your VAT return (monthly or quarterly CA3, annual CA12) in your professional account on impots.gouv.fr, then pay the balance before the deadline.
howTo.generic: Enter these amounts on your country's VAT return (online or at the tax office) and pay the balance before the deadline. If in doubt, have your accountant check them.
howTo.sources: How it is calculated: issued invoices (excluding drafts, quotes and cancellations without a credit note), minus credit notes issued, minus VAT on the period's purchase orders and expenses.

about.syscohada: SYSCOHADA: the common chart of accounts of the 17 OHADA countries (West and Central Africa). Classes 1 to 9, amounts in FCFA.
about.pcg: PCG: the French General Chart of Accounts, also used in Belgium and North Africa. Classes 1 to 7.
about.skr03: SKR03 (DATEV): the standard chart of accounts of German small businesses, known to every Steuerberater. 4-digit accounts; VAT per rate (Umsatzsteuer 1776/1771, Vorsteuer 1576/1571); amounts in euros.
